display.title: Shlomo HaMelech's Pool
display.summary_short: A wicked advisor tricks the king of Spain into ordering Rabbi Yehuda to build a copy of Shlomo HaMelech's pool, but Hashem's help turns every plot around.
display.summary_long: In a faraway city in Spain, the great scholar Rabbi Yehuda is the king's trusted chief advisor. The jealous advisor Ivan, who hates the Jews, persuades the king to have Rabbi Yehuda build a pool like Shlomo HaMelech's. After saying Tehillim, Rabbi Yehuda and his wife Sarah find the plans in her late father's chest, hidden deep beneath their house. The pool is built, but the gold paint keeps floating off, so Rabbi Yehuda cleverly hands the painting to Ivan, who secretly knows the trick. Ivan then has the king demand an oath that nothing was taken from the treasury. Rabbi Yehuda will not swear to what he cannot know for sure, and he is thrown into the river. A Jewish doctor, Rabbi Yitzchak, rescues him and hides him in his home. When the king loses his royal ring in the river, Ivan has him decree that the Jews must find it within 30 days or be expelled. The community fasts and says Tehillim, Rabbi Yehuda catches a fish with the ring inside, and a clever plan at the riverbank brings Rabbi Yehuda back to the palace and ends Ivan's schemes for good.
display.lesson: Hashem watches over the Jewish people at every moment; when trouble comes, daven and say Tehillim, never swear to something you are not sure of, and thank Hashem for what He gives us.

advisories.note: Rabbi Yehuda is sentenced to death, tied up and thrown into a river; a doctor rescues and revives him.
The king decrees that all the Jews will be expelled if they cannot find his lost ring.
At the end the villain is thrown into the river and does not come back.
